summary: Hello, we are the MarsGuard team. Our group consists of two members, along with our advisor, teacher Betül Küçükçakır. We have developed a system designed for the International Space Station (ISS) to monitor the health of astronauts while they engage in exercise, conduct research, or perform other tasks. The device measures heart rate, oxygen levels, the presence of various gases (both hazardous and non-hazardous), ambient light intensity, and temperature. It features a display screen, and a touch sensor allows users to navigate between different data pages. If any reading falls outside the normal range, the system provides an alert. The device can also be connected to a computer via a cable to view the data on a larger screen. We used an Arduino Uno to control and manage all functions, and we created a custom 3D-printed housing to hold the breadboard and the Arduino Uno. This device is designed to be worn on the arm. In the future, we plan to add more complex sensors and features, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and a Geiger counter for measuring radiation.
